FINAL YEAR PROJECT
Multimodal Satellite Image
Registration:
A Comparative Study of Classical
Feature-Based and Deep Learning Approaches
Multimodal Satellite Image Registration  |  NIT Warangal 1 / 13

Introduction & Motivation
Why Multimodal Satellite Image Registration Matters
Multimodal Satellite Image Registration  |  NIT Warangal 2 / 13
Domain Context
•  Earth observation satellite constellations are growing exponentially
•  Terabytes of multimodal remote sensing data generated daily
•  Sensors: Electro-Optical (EO), SAR, Infrared, Multispectral
•  Critical applications: change detection, disaster mapping, precision 
agriculture
•  Accurate spatial alignment is prerequisite for all downstream analyses
Research Gap & Motivation
•  Classical algorithms designed for same-sensor alignment
•  Cross-modal radiometry is non-linear & often inverted
•  A road bright in EO may appear dark in SAR imagery
•  Even 2–3 px misalignment causes significant GIS errors
•  No standardised benchmark comparing classical vs. DL methods
•  This project fills the gap with a six-algorithm comparative study

Problem Statement
Formal Definition of the Technical Challenge
Multimodal Satellite Image Registration  |  NIT Warangal 3 / 13
Systematically evaluate and compare multiple registration paradigms — from hand-crafted feature descriptors to deep-learning methods — applied to 
multimodal satellite image pairs (EO vs. SAR/NIR), using standardised metrics: Keypoint Count, Correct Matching Rate (CMR), and RMSE.
Primary Challenges
Challenge 1 — Cross-Modal Radiometric Inversion
Pixel intensity relationships are non-linear and often reversed between sensor types. Gradient-based descriptors produce opposite vectors for the same physical feature, collapsing 
descriptor similarity near zero.
Challenge 2 — Absence of Standardised Benchmarks
Existing literature evaluates algorithms in isolation. No standardised framework exists to compare SIFT, ORB, BRISK, SASF, CNN, and NN-DISK under identical preprocessing, RANSAC 
parameters, and matching thresholds.
Challenge 3 — Sub-pixel Accuracy Requirement
Professional GIS and photogrammetric applications demand RMSE ≤ 1 px. At 0.5 m/px GSD, even a 2 px error translates to a 1 m ground displacement, rendering cadastral and 
precision-agriculture analysis unreliable.

Literature Review & Background
Prior Art and Identified Research Gaps
Multimodal Satellite Image Registration  |  NIT Warangal 4 / 13
SIFT [Lowe, IJCV 2004]
128-D gradient histogram; scale & rotation invariant; fails on cross-modal intensity inversions.
ORB [Rublee et al., ICCV 2011]
256-bit rBRIEF; ~100× faster than SIFT; binary comparisons collapse under cross-modal domain 
shifts.
BRISK [Leutenegger et al., ICCV 2011]
512-bit ring-pattern binary; better discriminativity than ORB; same fundamental vulnerability to 
radiometric inversion.
SASF [Ye et al., IEEE T-GRS 2017]
60-D NCC self-convolution; designed for multimodal robustness; best classical CMR but still 
limited by hand-crafted invariance.
SuperPoint [DeTone et al., CVPR-W 2018]
Self-supervised joint detector-descriptor; demonstrated superiority of learned descriptors —
foundational for deep registration.
DISK [Tyszkiewicz et al., NeurIPS 2020]
RL-trained joint detector-descriptor; matchability-optimized keypoints; SOTA cross-modal 
registration accuracy.
Gap: No prior work performs a standardised 6-algorithm cross-paradigm comparison with identical conditions + geographic impact quantification.

Proposed Methodology & Architecture
End-to-End Feature-Based Registration Pipeline & DISK Neural Network
Multimodal Satellite Image Registration  |  NIT Warangal 5 / 13
Fig 1: General Feature-Based Registration Pipeline Fig 2: DISK U-Net Architecture (Encoder–Decoder + Dual Heads)
•  1. Image Pre-processing & Downscaling (max 2000 px)
•  2. Keypoint Detection (modality-specific detector)
•  3. Descriptor Extraction (hand-crafted || deep learned)
•  4. Feature Matching (L2/Hamming + Lowe's Ratio Test τ=0.75/0.9)
•  5. RANSAC Homography Estimation (threshold = 5.0 px)
•  6. Warping, Evaluation: CMR & RMSE

Implementation Details
Technical Stack, Mathematical Core, and Novel Modifications
Multimodal Satellite Image Registration  |  NIT Warangal 6 / 13
Technical Stack
•  Language: Python 3.9
•  Computer Vision: OpenCV 4.x (SIFT, ORB, BRISK, BFMatcher, RANSAC)
•  Deep Learning: PyTorch + Kornia (DISK model, match_snn)
•  Numerical: NumPy (NCC computation, descriptor assembly)
•  Visualisation: Matplotlib (CMR/RMSE bar charts)
•  Hardware: CPU inference; GPU-compatible (CUDA)
•  RANSAC threshold: 5.0 px | Ratio test: τ = 0.75 (classical), 0.9 (DISK)
Novel Technical Contributions
•  SASF implemented from scratch in Python (OpenCV has no native SASF)
•  NCC self-convolution over 4 rings × 16 angles → 64-D descriptor
•  Entropy-based saliency keypoint selection (top-80th percentile)
•  Dynamic image downscaling (INTER_AREA) prevents GPU OOM
•  Unified evaluation pipeline: same RANSAC params for all 6 methods
•  Geographic impact table: pixel RMSE → ground error (m) at 0.5 m GSD
•  Kornia match_snn Soft-Nearest-Neighbour for DISK cycle-consistent matching
SASF NCC:  φ(Rᵢ, Rⱼ) = Σ(Rᵢ·Rⱼ) / (‖Rᵢ‖·‖Rⱼ‖) DISK RL Reward:  R = Σinliers P(mᵢⱼ) − λ Σoutliers P(mᵢⱼ)

Experimental Setup & Datasets
Data, Evaluation Protocol, and Performance Metrics
Multimodal Satellite Image Registration  |  NIT Warangal 7 / 13
Image A — Electro-Optical (EO) Image B — Near-Infrared / SAR
Experimental Parameters
•  Image pair: EO vs. NIR/SAR (same scene, different sensors)
•  Downscale: max 2000 px (INTER_AREA)
•  RANSAC reproj. threshold: 5.0 px
•  Ratio test: τ = 0.75 (SIFT/ORB/BRISK/SASF), 0.9 (DISK)
•  Preprocessing: grayscale conversion + optional Gaussian blur
•  6 Algorithms: SIFT, ORB, BRISK, SASF, CNN, NN-DISK
Evaluation Metrics
• Keypoints (KP): Total keypoints detected in Image A and Image B.
• Correct Matching Rate (CMR = Mₒ / M × 100%): Fraction of putative matches surviving RANSAC as geometric inliers.  Higher is better.
• RMSE (px): Root Mean Square reprojection error of RANSAC inliers — quantifies sub-pixel geometric accuracy.  Lower is better.
• Geographic Error (m) = RMSE × GSD.  At 0.5 m/px GSD, RMSE = 1 px ≡ 0.5 m ground error.

Discussion & Comparative Performance
Why Deep Learning Dominates — Invariance Analysis
Multimodal Satellite Image Registration  |  NIT Warangal 9 / 13
Fig 5: Keypoints Detected vs. Correct Matches per Algorithm
Why NN-DISK Wins
•  ORB/BRISK: binary intensity comparisons flip sign under cross-modal inversion → CMR ~3%
•  SIFT: gradient histograms rotate 180° for same physical feature → CMR 8.5%
•  SASF: NCC captures structure (not intensity) → CMR 21.9% — best classical
•  DISK: joint RL training directly maximises correct matches — not a proxy loss
•  U-Net large receptive field encodes global structural context, not just local patch
•  Cycle-consistent SNN matching eliminates ambiguous pairs before RANSAC
•  DISK achieves 32.95× more correct matches than ORB (1,196 vs. 37)
•  RMSE 0.87 px: ONLY method meeting sub-pixel photogrammetric threshold

Limitations & Constraints
Critical Evaluation of Scope and Boundary Conditions
Multimodal Satellite Image Registration  |  NIT Warangal 10 / 13
⚠ Single Image Pair
Experiments conducted on one EO–NIR/SAR pair. Generalisation across heterogeneous datasets 
(multi-temporal, multi-geographic) cannot be guaranteed without broader validation.
⚠ Computational Cost — DISK
NN-DISK inference takes ~60 s on CPU for full-resolution satellite images. Classical methods 
(SIFT, ORB, BRISK) complete in <0.2 s. Real-time deployment requires GPU acceleration or 
model quantization.
⚠ SASF Python Implementation
Custom SASF is implemented in pure Python with NumPy loops. Native C++ implementation 
would be significantly faster; current runtime is ~6 s vs. <0.2 s for OpenCV-native methods.
⚠ Fixed Homography Model
A 3×3 projective homography assumes a planar scene. For high-relief terrain or large geographic 
extents, a non-rigid deformation model would be more appropriate.
⚠ No Domain Fine-Tuning
DISK weights are pretrained on generic image pairs, not specifically on satellite EO–SAR multimodal data. Fine-tuning on domain-specific data is expected to improve results further.

Conclusion
Core Technical Achievement and Impact
Multimodal Satellite Image Registration  |  NIT Warangal 11 / 13
① Deep Learning Achieves a Qualitative Leap
NN-DISK achieves CMR = 98.19% and RMSE = 0.87 px — the only method meeting the sub-pixel photogrammetric threshold. This represents a 32.95× improvement in correct matches 
and a 7× reduction in RMSE over the best classical method (SASF).
② SASF is the Recommended Classical Fallback
Among hand-crafted methods, SASF's NCC-based structural descriptor achieves CMR = 21.9% and RMSE = 2.81 px — nearly 3× better CMR than SIFT and 7× better than ORB. It is the 
recommended choice for constrained-compute environments where deep learning infrastructure is unavailable.
③ Data-Driven Features Fundamentally Outperform Hand-Crafted Invariances
This study empirically demonstrates that end-to-end RL-optimized feature learning produces cross-modal invariances that cannot be achieved through engineering alone. The gap is not 
marginal — it is a categorical performance difference that enables previously impossible applications (cadastral mapping, precision agriculture) from multimodal satellite data.

Future Scope
Logical Extensions and Research Roadmap
Multimodal Satellite Image Registration  |  NIT Warangal 12 / 13
→  Transformer-Based Matching (LightGlue)
Replace SNN matching with a Transformer matcher using self-attention and cross-attention for 
global, context-aware correspondence — expected to further reduce false matches in 
repetitive-texture regions.
→  Domain-Specific Fine-Tuning
Fine-tune DISK on curated Sentinel-1 SAR + Sentinel-2 optical multimodal pairs. Domain-specific 
training is projected to push CMR beyond 99% and RMSE below 0.5 px for common satellite 
sensor combinations.
→  Tiled Inference for Very Large Images
Develop a tiled inference pipeline supporting images >10,000 px without resolution 
degradation, overcoming GPU memory constraints through overlapping tile stitching and 
descriptor interpolation.
→  Open-Set Recognition Integration
Incorporate open-set keypoint rejection (CroR-OSIR, CVPR 2025) to proactively reject 
unmatchable keypoints before matching, improving CMR on extreme cross-modal pairs with low 
structural overlap.
→  Real-Time Edge Deployment
Quantise NN-DISK to INT8/FP16 and compile with TensorRT for deployment on edge computing platforms (NVIDIA Jetson) at >20 fps, enabling onboard satellite or UAV registration.
